title: Force and Motion
description: Forces can be balanced or unbalanced. Unbalanced forces cause objects to speed up, slow down, or change direction. Mass and force both affect motion.

exercises.question: What happens when forces on an object are BALANCED?
choices: the object does not change its motion
exercises.exp: Balanced forces cancel each other out — the object stays still or keeps moving at the same speed.

exercises.question: What happens when forces on an object are UNBALANCED?
choices: the object changes its speed or direction
exercises.exp: Unbalanced forces cause a change in motion — speeding up, slowing down, or changing direction.

exercises.question: A book sitting still on a table has balanced forces. Which forces are balanced?
choices: gravity pulling down AND the table pushing up
exercises.exp: Gravity pulls the book down; the table pushes up equally — balanced forces keep the book still.

exercises.question: You push a toy car with TWICE the force. What happens to the car's speed?
exercises.exp: More force = more acceleration. Double the force and the car speeds up much more!

exercises.question: A heavier ball and a lighter ball are pushed with the same force. Which moves FASTER?
exercises.exp: Less mass = more acceleration with the same force. The lighter ball will move faster!

exercises.question: FRICTION is a force that ___.
choices: slows objects down and produces heat
exercises.exp: Friction opposes motion between surfaces — it slows things down and turns energy into heat.

exercises.question: Which surface would have the MOST friction?
exercises.exp: Rough concrete creates lots of friction — that is why cars stop faster on concrete than on ice!

exercises.question: GRAVITY is a force that ___.
choices: pulls all objects with mass toward each other
exercises.exp: Gravity pulls all objects with mass toward each other. On Earth, everything is pulled toward Earth's centre.

exercises.question: A car brakes suddenly and the passenger lurches FORWARD. This happens because ___.
choices: the passenger is pushed forward by the seat
the passenger's body wants to keep moving forward (inertia)
exercises.exp: Inertia means objects in motion tend to stay in motion — your body keeps moving forward even when the car stops!

exercises.question: Compare speeds: A snail travels 10 cm in 1 minute. A rabbit travels 60 m in 1 minute. Which is faster?
exercises.exp: 60 metres vs 0.1 metres per minute — the rabbit is 600 times faster! Speed = distance ÷ time.

exercises.question: When you RUB your hands together quickly, they get warm. This is because ___.
choices: friction converts motion energy into heat energy
air between hands heats up by itself
skin produces heat naturally when pressed
exercises.exp: Friction between your palms converts kinetic (motion) energy into thermal (heat) energy — that is why they warm up!

exercises.question: Which example shows an UNBALANCED force changing motion?
choices: a parked car with engine off
a goalkeeper kicking a stationary ball into motion
two teams in a tug-of-war pulling equally
exercises.exp: The goalkeeper's kick applies an unbalanced force to the still ball — it changes from not moving to moving fast!

exercises.question: What is INERTIA?
choices: a force that speeds things up
the tendency of an object to resist changes to its state of motion
exercises.exp: Inertia is the tendency of objects to keep doing what they are already doing — staying still or moving in a straight line unless a force acts.

exercises.question: A ball rolls off a table and curves DOWNWARD to the floor. Which force causes the downward curve?
exercises.exp: Gravity pulls the ball downward as it moves forward — the combination of forward motion and downward gravity creates the curved path.

exercises.question: Speed is calculated as ___.
exercises.exp: Speed = distance ÷ time. If you travel 100 m in 10 seconds, your speed is 100÷10 = 10 m/s.

exercises.question: A car travels 200 km in 4 hours. What is its average speed?
exercises.exp: Speed = distance ÷ time = 200 km ÷ 4 h = 50 km/h.

exercises.question: ACCELERATION means an object is ___.
exercises.exp: Acceleration includes speeding up, slowing down, or changing direction — any change in velocity is acceleration!

exercises.question: A sled on SMOOTH ICE travels farther than on ROUGH SNOW with the same push. Why?
choices: ice has less friction than rough snow — less force slows the sled
snow is softer so the sled sinks
exercises.exp: Less friction on ice means less opposing force — the sled maintains its speed longer before stopping.

exercises.question: When you DROP a ball, gravity pulls it DOWN. Air RESISTANCE pushes UP. If air resistance equals gravity, the ball ___.
exercises.exp: When gravity (down) = air resistance (up), forces are balanced — the ball stops accelerating and falls at a constant terminal velocity.

exercises.question: Two students push a box from OPPOSITE sides with EQUAL force. The box ___.
choices: does not move — forces are balanced
exercises.exp: Equal forces from opposite directions cancel out — net force is zero, so the box does not move. Balanced forces!

exercises.question: A HEAVIER cart is harder to push and stop than a lighter cart. This is because of ___.
choices: more inertia — greater mass resists changes to motion more strongly
less gravity on the lighter cart
the heavier cart has magnetic properties
exercises.exp: Inertia increases with mass — heavier objects resist changes in motion more. More force is needed to accelerate or stop them.

exercises.question: What is a NET FORCE?
choices: the total combined force on an object after all forces are added together
the force a net makes when thrown
exercises.exp: Net force is all forces combined. Two forces pulling opposite ways: subtract. Same direction: add. Net force determines acceleration.

exercises.question: A 10 N force pushes RIGHT and a 4 N force pushes LEFT on a box. What is the net force and direction?
exercises.exp: 10N right − 4N left = 6N net force to the right. The box accelerates right.

exercises.question: STREAMLINING a car's shape (making it smooth and tapered) helps reduce ___.
exercises.exp: A streamlined shape lets air flow smoothly around the car, reducing drag (air resistance) — making it faster and more fuel-efficient.

exercises.question: A skydiver opens a PARACHUTE. They slow down quickly. Why?
choices: gravity decreases when the parachute opens
the parachute greatly increases air resistance, creating an upward force larger than gravity for a moment
the parachute pushes on the ground
exercises.exp: A large parachute catches air — huge air resistance pushes up against the falling skydiver, rapidly slowing them to a safe landing speed.

exercises.question: Lubrication (adding OIL or GREASE) to a machine ___.
choices: decreases friction, reducing wear and allowing smoother motion
exercises.exp: Oil fills the microscopic gaps between surfaces — fewer surface-to-surface contacts means much less friction. This reduces wear and energy loss!

exercises.question: A shopping cart is pushed across a FLAT floor at constant speed. The pushing force must equal ___.
choices: zero — no force needed for constant speed
exercises.exp: Constant speed = balanced forces. The push equals friction (air resistance + wheel friction) exactly — net force is zero.

exercises.question: Which situation has the MOST friction?
choices: a rubber eraser dragged across sandpaper
a bar of soap on a wet tile
exercises.exp: Both surfaces are rough (rubber + sandpaper = high friction). Ice, glass, and wet soap are all very smooth — low friction!

exercises.question: A student pushes a block with 15 N. Friction is 5 N opposing motion. What is the net force?
exercises.exp: Net force = 15N push − 5N friction = 10N forward. The block accelerates forward.

exercises.question: SEAT BELTS in cars protect passengers because ___.
choices: they add extra weight to keep passengers down
they act as a force to stop passengers flying forward when the car stops suddenly (overcoming inertia)
they reduce friction in the car
they connect passengers to the car's engine
exercises.exp: When a car stops suddenly, inertia keeps passengers moving forward. Seat belts exert a backward force to stop them from flying through the windshield!

exercises.question: ROLLING FRICTION is generally ___ than SLIDING friction.
choices: smaller — that is why wheels were invented!
variable — it depends on the day
exercises.exp: Rolling friction is much smaller than sliding friction — wheels roll with tiny contact area and much less resistance. That is why wheels revolutionised transport!

exercises.question: Earth's GRAVITY pulls all objects with the same acceleration (ignoring air resistance) — about 9.8 m/s² downward. If you drop a feather and a rock in a VACUUM, they ___.
choices: both fall at exactly the same rate
exercises.exp: Without air resistance, all objects fall at the same rate regardless of mass — as Galileo famously showed. In a vacuum, feather = rock!

exercises.question: NEWTON'S SECOND LAW states that force equals ___.
exercises.exp: F = ma: Force = mass × acceleration. Double the force and the acceleration doubles. Double the mass and acceleration halves. Foundational physics!

exercises.question: A 2 kg ball is pushed with 10 N of force. What is its acceleration?
exercises.exp: a = F ÷ m = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 m/s². Using Newton's 2nd Law: force divided by mass gives acceleration.

exercises.question: NEWTON'S THIRD LAW states that ___.
choices: every action force has an equal and opposite reaction force
only balanced forces can cause motion
exercises.exp: Newton's 3rd: for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. Rocket exhaust pushes down → rocket is pushed up. Swimmer pushes water back → water pushes swimmer forward!

exercises.question: MOMENTUM = mass × velocity. Which object has MORE momentum?
choices: a 1 kg ball at 10 m/s (p = 10 kg·m/s)
a 5 kg ball at 3 m/s (p = 15 kg·m/s)
a 0.5 kg ball at 20 m/s (p = 10 kg·m/s)
a 2 kg ball at 4 m/s (p = 8 kg·m/s)
exercises.exp: Momentum = mass × velocity. 5 × 3 = 15 kg·m/s is the largest. A heavy slow truck has more momentum than a fast tennis ball!

exercises.question: What is WORK in physics?
choices: force applied over a distance: W = force × distance (only when force moves in the direction of motion)
the energy stored in an object
exercises.exp: Work = Force × Distance. Pushing a box 5m with 10N force = 50 joules of work. If the box does not move, NO work is done (regardless of effort)!

exercises.question: Which has MORE kinetic energy?
exercises.exp: KE = ½mv². A fast-moving train has both large mass AND high speed — giving it enormous kinetic energy compared to the golf ball or parked car!

exercises.question: POTENTIAL ENERGY depends on ___.
choices: position relative to a reference point — higher position = more gravitational potential energy
exercises.exp: Gravitational PE = mgh (mass × gravity × height). A ball held high has more PE than the same ball held low — it can do more work when released!

exercises.question: A ball rolls off a table. As it falls, its potential energy ___.
choices: decreases while its kinetic energy increases
decreases while its kinetic energy also decreases
exercises.exp: As height decreases, PE (mgh) decreases. That energy converts to kinetic energy (motion). Total mechanical energy is conserved (ignoring air resistance)!

exercises.question: What is TERMINAL VELOCITY?
choices: the maximum speed a car can reach
the speed at which an object's weight equals air resistance — net force is zero, so speed stays constant
the speed at first contact with the ground
the initial speed when dropped from height
exercises.exp: Terminal velocity: gravity pulling down equals air resistance pushing up → net force = 0 → constant speed. Skydivers reach about 55 m/s (200 km/h)!

exercises.question: SIMPLE MACHINES make work EASIER by changing ___.
choices: the direction or magnitude of forces needed (reducing force required or changing direction)
exercises.exp: Simple machines (levers, pulleys, ramps) change the size or direction of forces. You can lift heavy objects with less force — but over a greater distance. Work done stays the same!

exercises.question: A pulley system with 4 ropes supporting a load reduces the force needed by ___.
choices: 4 times — mechanical advantage equals number of supporting rope segments
exercises.exp: Mechanical advantage of a pulley = number of rope segments supporting the load. 4 ropes = you only need 1/4 of the force to lift the object!

exercises.question: A car moving at 100 km/h hits the brakes. What force decelerates it?
choices: friction between tyres and road, and friction in the brakes
the normal force from the road surface
exercises.exp: Braking friction from tyres+road and internal brake friction convert kinetic energy to heat — slowing the car. No friction = no braking (ice)!

exercises.question: CENTRIPETAL FORCE is the force that ___.
choices: pushes objects outward from a circular path
acts inward toward the centre of a circular path, keeping objects moving in a circle
exercises.exp: Centripetal means 'centre-seeking.' This inward force keeps objects on circular paths — gravity keeps Earth orbiting the sun; string keeps a ball spinning in circles!

exercises.question: Which of Newton's Laws explains why you should wear a seatbelt?
choices: Newton's 1st Law (inertia) — the car stops but your body tends to keep moving forward
exercises.exp: Newton's 1st (inertia): your body tends to keep moving forward when the car suddenly stops. The seatbelt exerts a backward force to stop you from flying forward!

exercises.question: What is POWER in physics?
choices: the rate of doing work: Power = Work ÷ Time (measured in watts)
the force applied to an object
exercises.exp: Power = Work / Time. A powerful engine does more work per second. 1 watt = 1 joule per second. A 100W light bulb uses 100 joules every second!

exercises.question: Why is it EASIER to push a car on a smooth concrete floor than on rough gravel?
choices: smooth concrete has less friction — less force needed to overcome friction and move the car
the car weighs less on concrete
exercises.exp: Rough gravel has more surface irregularities → more friction → more force needed. Smooth concrete has less friction → easier to push!

exercises.question: EFFICIENCY is how much input energy becomes useful output energy. Most car engines are only about 25% efficient. This means ___.
choices: 75% of fuel energy is wasted as heat and sound, not used for motion
exercises.exp: 75% of fuel energy in petrol engines is lost as heat (exhaust, friction, cooling). Only 25% moves the car. Engineers work to improve efficiency!

exercises.question: Which simple machine would make it EASIEST to move a heavy barrel from ground level into a truck?
choices: an inclined plane (ramp) — spreading the work over a longer distance reduces the force needed
a pulley fixed to the sky
exercises.exp: An inclined plane lets you push the barrel up a long gradual ramp — less force over more distance. The same work is done, just with less force!

exercises.question: The COEFFICIENT OF FRICTION between two surfaces tells you ___.
choices: the ratio of friction force to normal force — how much friction you get per unit of perpendicular force
the weight of one surface on the other
exercises.exp: μ (coefficient of friction) = friction force ÷ normal force. Ice has μ ≈ 0.03 (very slippery). Rubber on dry road ≈ 0.7 (good grip)!
